when bumping into a secret wall, instead of "needing" to do search, let people that bump into the wall three times discover the door with good messgaes.

ignite weapons does not appear to be working, or, it should have a much higher chance to apply burning; and, it should show the usual flaming weapon "thing" -- like envenomed does.

commit and bump and push when ready

I’m going to trace the existing secret-wall search/discovery and envenomed/ignite status paths, then implement both changes with focused tests, bump `VERSION`, run the relevant guardrails, and commit/push on `master`. I’m using the repo’s `agent-tools` and `using-entire` guidance to preserve the project’s architecture and checkpoint history.

content.text: The working tree is currently clean, so there are no user edits to preserve. The existing secret-door path confirms the issue: only the search resolver reveals or hints at doors, while blocked movement has no secret-door state transition. Ignite already creates a temporary effect, but melee applies burn at only 20% and does not emit the visual/status event used by the envenomed presentation. I’m tracing those exact contracts now before patching.

content.text: The implementation is now wired in the canonical bump resolver and weapon-affinity/effect definitions. One important runtime issue surfaced while tracing: Ignite’s burn branch only wrote to an already-present legacy `ActiveEffects` array, so targets without that component could never burn. I’m correcting it to use the existing effect initializer, then I’ll run the focused movement/combat/visual tests and adjust any boundary issues they expose.

content.text: Focused behavior tests pass after fixing a shared constant regression exposed by the movement suite. Ignite now initializes the target’s effects when needed, reads its authored `bonusFireDamage`/`burnChance`, applies canonical `burning`, emits `proc:ignited`, and resolves `ignite_weapons` to the same flame weapon VFX affinity as envenomed weapons do for poison. `VERSION` is already at `0.9.1384` in `HEAD`, so I’ll keep that existing bump and verify the final diff before committing.

content.text: The new Ignite regression test caught the real failure: the existing bonus-fire call referenced an undefined `spec`, so the attack aborted before the burn logic. I’m fixing that to use the already-computed defender position; this explains why the spell appeared completely inert in play.

All focused tests and architecture/event guardrails are green, and `git diff --check` is clean. I’ve bumped `VERSION` from `0.9.1384` to `0.9.1385`; I’m committing the nine-file change now, then I’ll push `master` as requested.
